title: Safety Insurance Q3 Profit Rises as Mapfre Deal Nears Closing
summary: Safety Insurance Group reported third-quarter 2026 net income of $30.0 million ($2.05 a share) and a combined ratio of 96.3%, while its $1.54 billion cash sale to Mapfre at $105 a share cleared a shareholder vote on November 3 and awaits Massachusetts regulatory approval.
description:
Safety Insurance Group, a Massachusetts-based property and casualty insurer listed on Nasdaq under the symbol SAFT, released its third-quarter 2026 results on November 4, 2026. The report arrived one day after the company's shareholders approved a cash takeover by an affiliate of Mapfre S.A., the Spanish insurance group. That timing makes the quarter unusual: it is both an ordinary set of earnings and one of the last reports Safety is expected to publish as an independent public company. This article sets out what the earnings release says, then explains the terms of the Mapfre transaction as they were announced.

The quarter in numbers

Net income for the third quarter was $30.0 million, or $2.05 per diluted share, compared with $28.3 million, or $1.91 per share, in the same quarter of 2025. That is an increase of about 6% in net income, calculated here. The company also reports a non-GAAP operating income measure that strips out certain investment and other items. On that basis, operating income was $28.6 million, or $1.95 per diluted share, against $21.9 million, or $1.48 per share, a year earlier, an increase of roughly 30% in total dollars, calculated here.

Net written premiums, the premiums an insurer keeps after paying for reinsurance, were $296.2 million, down 4.2% from $309.2 million. Direct written premiums, the premiums written before reinsurance, were $319.7 million, down 4.3% from $334.2 million. Premium volume therefore shrank by a little over four percent while profit rose, which is a pattern that can occur when an insurer prices for profit rather than growth, although the release does not frame it that way.

Underwriting results

The combined ratio, which adds claims costs and operating expenses and divides them by premiums earned, improved to 96.3% from 98.9%. A figure below 100% means the insurer earned more in premiums than it paid out in losses and expenses. The improvement of 2.6 percentage points, calculated here, came entirely from the loss side. The loss ratio fell to 67.2% from 70.4%, while the expense ratio rose to 29.1% from 28.5%.

George M. Murphy, Safety's chairman, president and chief executive, attributed the lower losses in part to "improved loss frequency in our private passenger automobile line." Loss frequency is how often policyholders make claims. Fewer claims per insured vehicle is a direct benefit to an auto insurer, because severity, the cost of each claim, tends to be less controllable. The release also reports favorable development on prior-year claims, meaning earlier loss estimates proved slightly too high, of $10.1 million before tax, compared with $9.7 million a year earlier. Reserve releases of that size help the quarter, and readers should note that they are separate from current-year underwriting.

The release does not disclose a figure for catastrophe losses in the third quarter. It does attribute the weaker year-to-date result to two severe winter weather events in the first quarter of 2026.

Investment income reaches a record

Net investment income rose 15.0% to $17.9 million, from $15.5 million. The net effective annualized portfolio yield was 4.2%, up from 4.0%. Mr. Murphy described the quarter's net investment income as "the largest quarterly net investment income results in our Company's history." Higher yields on bonds purchased in recent years, combined with a growing portfolio, have been lifting investment income at many insurers, and Safety's figures follow that pattern.

The nine-month picture

The first nine months are less favorable. Net income for the period was $50.2 million, or $3.43 per diluted share, against $79.1 million, or $5.33 per share, a fall of about 37% in net income, calculated here. Non-GAAP operating income per diluted share was $3.28, compared with $4.19. Net written premiums for the nine months were $885.1 million, down 2.0%. The nine-month combined ratio was 101.7%, against 98.9% a year earlier, with the loss ratio at 73.0% against 69.7% and the expense ratio at 28.7% against 29.2%. Losses and loss adjustment expenses incurred were $640.2 million, up 8.6%. Net investment income for the nine months was $51.5 million, up 12.3%.

In other words, a strong third quarter has partly offset a first quarter in which storms pushed the combined ratio above 100%. The company's own earlier releases, summarized in the merger announcement, showed a combined ratio of 99.0% for the full year 2025, against 101.1% in 2024, and 95.7% for the second quarter of 2026.

Dividend and book value

The board declared a quarterly dividend of $0.92 per share, payable on December 15, 2026 to shareholders of record on December 1, 2026. Book value per share was $58.29 at September 30, 2026, compared with $60.98 at December 31, 2025. The decline over nine months reflects, among other things, the lower earnings in the first half, although the release should be consulted for the full reconciliation.

The Mapfre transaction

On July 23, 2026, Safety announced that it had agreed to be acquired by an affiliate of Mapfre for $105 per share in cash, a deal valued at about $1.54 billion. Under the structure announced, a subsidiary of Mapfre U.S.A. Corp. will merge into Safety, which will become a wholly owned subsidiary of Mapfre U.S.A. Corp. The announcement described the price as a premium of 44% to Safety's share price. Dividing the deal value by the price implies roughly 14.7 million shares, and the price is about 1.8 times the September 30 book value per share, both calculated here.

The agreement was approved unanimously by Safety's board. Shareholders voted to approve it on November 3, 2026. It still requires prior approval from the Massachusetts Commissioner of Insurance, the expiry or termination of any Hart-Scott-Rodino antitrust waiting period, and customary closing conditions. Both companies expected the transaction to close in the first quarter of 2027. Safety said it would keep its brand, its relationships with policyholders and independent agents, and its local market capabilities, and that its management team would continue to play an important role. Jefferies acted as Safety's financial adviser and DLA Piper as its legal adviser. The announcement did not describe how Mapfre will fund the purchase or disclose termination fees.

What to watch next

For readers following the deal, the key step is regulatory approval in Massachusetts, which has a tightly regulated personal auto market. Investors who hold the shares will also look at whether the quarterly dividend continues until closing, as the declared $0.92 payment suggests for now. For customers, the company has said that policies, agents and the Safety brand are expected to remain in place after the sale.

Sources: Safety Insurance Group's third-quarter 2026 earnings release filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on November 4, 2026, and the company's July 23, 2026 merger announcement with Mapfre. Figures labelled as calculated here are derived from the reported numbers and are not company statements.

key_points: Third-quarter net income was $30.0 million, or $2.05 a diluted share, against $28.3 million, or $1.91, a year earlier, and non-GAAP operating income per share rose to $1.95 from $1.48.
The combined ratio improved to 96.3% from 98.9%, with the loss ratio falling to 67.2% from 70.4% and the expense ratio rising to 29.1% from 28.5%.
Net written premiums fell 4.2% to $296.2 million, while net investment income rose 15.0% to $17.9 million, which the chief executive called the largest quarterly figure in the company's history.
Nine-month net income was $50.2 million against $79.1 million, and the nine-month combined ratio was 101.7%, reflecting two severe winter weather events in the first quarter.

why_it_matters: Safety is one of the larger auto and home insurers in Massachusetts and New England, so its results show how a regional personal lines carrier is performing after a winter of heavy storm losses. The pending sale to Mapfre also shows that a European group is willing to pay a large premium for a US personal lines franchise with a stable agency distribution base.

title: Trisura Q3 Net Income Falls 32% as Combined Ratio Hits 87.5%
summary: Trisura Group's third-quarter 2026 net income fell to C$26.2 million (C$0.54 a share) from C$38.6 million, but operating net income held at C$35.0 million and net insurance revenue from primary lines grew 12.5%, while the combined ratio rose to 87.5%.
description:
Trisura Group Ltd., a specialty insurance company listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange under the symbol TSU, reported its third-quarter 2026 results on November 5, 2026. The company writes surety, corporate insurance, programs and fronting business in Canada and the United States. Its results are reported in Canadian dollars. This article reports the figures from the company's release and explains the terms it uses, with calculations of growth rates marked as made here.

Headline results

Net income for the third quarter was $26.2 million, or $0.54 per diluted share, against $38.6 million, or $0.79 per share, in the third quarter of 2025. That is a decline of about 32% in net income, calculated here. The company also reports operating net income, a measure that adjusts for items management considers outside its ordinary operations. On that basis, the quarter produced $35.0 million, or $0.73 per diluted share, against $34.4 million, or $0.71 per share. Operating net income was therefore close to flat, up about 2% in dollars, calculated here, while net income fell sharply.

The difference between the two measures in the third quarter was roughly $8.8 million, calculated here by subtracting net income from operating net income. The release should be consulted for the specific items that account for that gap. The practical point for readers is that the underlying earnings power described by the company was stable, even though the number at the bottom of the income statement was lower.

Chief executive David Clare said that "Operating net income was stable at $35 million in the quarter," adding that growth in net investment income offset weaker casualty results in the company's US programs business.

Revenue, premiums and underwriting

Insurance revenue, which is the premium recognized as earned under the new insurance accounting standard, was $815.7 million against $776.5 million, an increase of about 5%, calculated here. Net insurance revenue, which is the portion retained after reinsurance ceded to others, was $203.1 million against $197.3 million, up about 3%, calculated here. The difference between the two lines is large because Trisura's fronting business passes most of its risk to reinsurers while keeping a fee and a retained share.

Gross premiums written, which measure the volume of new business before reinsurance, were $801.6 million, down from $853.7 million, a decrease of about 6%, calculated here. The insurance service result, which is revenue less claims and expenses on the standard's terms, was $31.8 million against $36.3 million, and underwriting income was $25.2 million against $27.6 million.

The combined ratio was 87.5% against 86.0% a year earlier. The loss ratio was 36.4%, up from 34.3%, and the expense ratio was 51.1%, down from 51.7%. A combined ratio below 100% means the business earned more in premiums than it paid in claims and expenses. Trisura's expense ratio can look high next to many property and casualty insurers, and its loss ratio low, because in fronting much of the claims risk is passed to reinsurers. For that reason, Trisura's combined ratio is better compared with its own history than with a conventional auto or home insurer.

Primary lines drive the growth

The release highlights primary lines, the segments in which Trisura keeps more risk on its own balance sheet, as the strongest part of the quarter. Net insurance revenue from primary lines grew 12.5% for the quarter and 10.1% for the nine months. Underwriting income from primary lines rose 15.5% in the quarter and 9.6% for the nine months. The chief executive said that "Our Primary lines continued to build momentum, with Net insurance revenue growing 12.5%." The company credited better profitability in US surety and US corporate insurance. By contrast, net insurance revenue in Canadian fronting declined, and casualty results in US programs were weaker.

The release does not provide separate combined ratios for each segment, so the figures above are for the company as a whole.

Investment income and book value

Net investment income increased to $23.8 million from $20.1 million, a rise of about 18%, calculated here. That growth helped offset the weaker underwriting in some segments. Book value per share was $20.93, against $18.90 a year earlier, an increase of 10.7%. The company noted that book value was slightly lower than at the end of the second quarter, which it attributed to unrealized losses on investments. Return on equity was 15.1%, unchanged from a year earlier, while operating return on equity fell to 16.2% from 18.0%. The debt-to-capital ratio rose to 17.4% from 13.0%.

Nine-month results

For the first nine months of 2026, net income was $106.4 million, or $2.21 per diluted share, compared with $104.7 million, or $2.16, a year earlier. Operating net income was $109.7 million, or $2.27 per share, against $101.9 million, or $2.10. Insurance revenue was $2,385.8 million against $2,314.9 million, and gross premiums written were $2,404.3 million against $2,465.8 million. Net insurance revenue rose to $595.1 million from $565.8 million. The nine-month combined ratio was 85.5%, against 84.9%, with a loss ratio of 34.4% and an expense ratio of 51.1%. Net investment income was $67.3 million against $57.2 million.

Over nine months, then, net income is slightly ahead of the prior year and operating net income is about 8% higher, calculated here, even though the third quarter on its own was weaker on a reported basis.

How to read the quarter

Three points stand out. First, the business mix is shifting toward primary lines, which carry more risk and, when they perform, more earnings. Second, casualty results in the US programs business were weaker, and casualty is a line where many insurers have been strengthening their reserves in recent years, so the segment will be worth watching in later quarters. Third, the rising debt-to-capital ratio, from 13.0% to 17.4%, shows that the company is using more borrowing as it grows, which is not unusual but changes the risk profile compared with a year ago.

Sources: Trisura Group Ltd. third-quarter 2026 results, issued through GlobeNewswire on November 5, 2026. Amounts are in Canadian dollars. Growth rates labelled as calculated here are derived from the reported figures and are not company statements.

Operating net income was stable at $35.0 million ($0.73 a share) against $34.4 million ($0.71), and operating return on equity was 16.2% against 18.0%.

why_it_matters: Trisura is a Toronto-listed specialty insurer that writes surety, corporate insurance and fronting in Canada and the United States, so its results show how a growing specialty carrier is coping with softer casualty experience and a shift in its business mix. The gap between net income and operating net income is also a reminder that the headline figure and the underlying figure can tell different stories.

title: Niva Bupa Q2 Profit Jumps 124% as Premiums Grow 35%
summary: Niva Bupa Health Insurance reported September-quarter profit after tax of about ₹136 crore, up 124%, on gross written premium of ₹2,484 crore, up 35%, with the combined operating ratio improving to 93.2% from 96.6% and retail health premium up 47%.
description:
Niva Bupa Health Insurance Company, one of India's standalone health insurers, announced its results for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026 on November 4, 2026. The company's board approved the unaudited results that day. This article reports the figures from the company's press release filed with the National Stock Exchange and from published coverage of the detailed results, and it identifies which source each number comes from, because the press release and the coverage report different measures in a few places.

Profit and premium

Profit after tax for the quarter was about ₹136 crore. Coverage of the detailed filing gives the exact figure as ₹135.64 crore, compared with ₹60.52 crore in the same quarter of the previous financial year. That is an increase of about 124%, which matches the company's own description. Profit before tax was ₹181.53 crore, against ₹81.74 crore. One crore is ten million, so ₹136 crore is about 1.36 billion rupees.

Gross written premium, the total premium booked before reinsurance, was ₹2,484 crore, up 35% from about ₹1,843 crore. For the first half of the year, published coverage reports gross written premium of ₹4,634 crore, up 33.4%. Insurance revenue, which is the premium recognized as earned under the Indian Accounting Standards that the company adopted from April 2026, was ₹2,412.27 crore against ₹1,899.07 crore, an increase of about 27%, calculated here. The insurance service result, the profit from insurance contracts before investment income, rose to ₹125.99 crore from ₹45.54 crore.

Retail health, the segment in which individuals and families buy their own policies, grew faster than the total. The press release states retail health gross written premium was ₹1,876 crore, up 47%, and that the company's market share in retail health was 11% at the end of the first half.

Claims, expenses and margins

The claims ratio, claims as a share of insurance revenue, improved to 63.09% from 65.08%. The expense ratio fell to 30.10% from 31.53%. Together they give a combined operating ratio of 93.20%, compared with 96.62% a year earlier, an improvement of about 3.4 percentage points, calculated here. A ratio below 100% means the insurer's claims and costs were less than the premium revenue it recognized in the period. The insurance service margin was 6.80%, against 3.38%, and the net insurance margin was 11.84%, against 10.27%.

The coverage reports two return measures that are not directly comparable. A quarterly return on equity of 3.53%, against 1.75%, appears in the detailed results. The press release gives an annualized return on average net worth of 14.7% for the first half, against 7.8% a year earlier. The second figure is annualized and the first is not, which explains most of the difference in appearance.

Claims service

The press release gives a number of operating indicators. The claim settlement ratio for the first half of the financial year was 95.6%, compared with 94.4% for the full previous year. More than 90% of cashless claims were processed in under 30 minutes, and more than 39% of claims were auto-adjudicated using artificial intelligence, meaning a system approved them without manual review. The company reports a weighted episodal net promoter score of 63, up six points, and a cashless discharge score of 74, up ten points, based on feedback from more than 1.9 lakh customers.

These are company-reported measures. Net promoter scores and settlement ratios are not audited and are defined by each insurer, so they are best used to compare a company with its own earlier periods.

Distribution and scale

Individual agents were the largest sales channel, at 34% of gross written premium in the quarter, while the direct channel was the fastest growing, up 46%. As of September 30, 2026, the company's distribution network included about 2.7 lakh agents, more than 620 brokers, and more than 135 bancassurance and other corporate agency partners, plus over 225 physical branches. The hospital and provider network exceeded 16,000. The company said it serves close to 27 million lives and has about 11,200 employees.

Vishwanath Mahendra, the company's executive director and chief financial officer, said the focus remains on pursuing profitable growth while continuing to improve operating efficiencies, according to the press release.

Solvency and the regulatory order

Coverage of the detailed results reports a solvency ratio of 2.03 against 2.85 a year earlier. The solvency ratio compares an insurer's available capital with the capital its regulator requires, and the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India sets a minimum of 1.5. A ratio of 2.03 is comfortably above the minimum, but the decline over the year shows that fast premium growth uses up capital. The press release itself reports a different measure, a combined insurance solvency ratio of 98.8%, which is not described further and should not be compared with the 2.03 figure.

The same coverage says the regulator ordered the company not to open new places of business for six months over limits on expenses of management in the 2024-25 financial year, and that the company accepted the order and will not appeal. It also says the company reported compliance with the expenses-of-management limits for the second quarter and the first half of 2026-27. The press release does not mention the order, so readers should check the company's stock exchange filings for the original wording.

Market reaction

Shares closed at ₹78.19 on the NSE on November 4, up 6.6% on the day, according to coverage of the results. The time stamp on the exchange filing suggests the results were filed in the evening India time, after that day's close, so the November 4 move should not be read as a reaction to them. A share price is in any case not a measure of the quality of a quarter.

What to watch

Three questions follow from the quarter. Can the company keep premium growth in the mid-thirties while holding the combined operating ratio below 95%? How will the solvency ratio move as growth continues and whether the company needs to raise capital? And how will the restriction on new places of business affect branch-led growth, given that agents and the direct channel already account for a large share of sales? The next set of quarterly results will show whether the improvement in margins is lasting.

Sources: Niva Bupa Health Insurance Company's press release on Q2 and H1 FY27 results, filed with the National Stock Exchange of India on November 4, 2026, and published coverage of the detailed results by Kotak Neo and Investywise. Growth rates labelled as calculated here are derived from the reported figures.

key_points: Profit after tax was about ₹136 crore (₹135.64 crore in the detailed filing) against ₹60.52 crore a year earlier, an increase of roughly 124%.
Gross written premium rose 35% to ₹2,484 crore, and retail health premium grew 47% to ₹1,876 crore, according to the company's press release.
The combined operating ratio improved to 93.20% from 96.62%, with the claims ratio at 63.09% and the expense ratio at 30.10%, as reported in coverage of the filing.
Claim settlement ratio for the first half was 95.6%, more than 90% of cashless claims were processed in under 30 minutes and about 39% of claims were auto-adjudicated using AI.
Reports of the filing say the solvency ratio fell to 2.03 from 2.85 a year earlier, and that an IRDAI order restricts new places of business for six months over past expense limits.
why_it_matters: Health insurance is the fastest-growing part of India's insurance market, and standalone health insurers such as Niva Bupa are the main way many households buy cover outside employer schemes. The quarter shows a rapid premium expansion paired with better claims and expense ratios, but also a lower solvency margin and a regulatory restriction that investors will track.

title: ICICI Life H1 Profit Up 26% as Protection Sales Surge
summary: ICICI Life Insurance, formerly ICICI Prudential Life, reported first-half FY27 profit of ₹760 crore, up 26.5%, with value of new business up 22.3% to ₹1,283 crore, a margin of 26%, and protection sales up 39.5% as solvency rose to 229.9%.
description:
ICICI Life Insurance, which was known as ICICI Prudential Life Insurance until earlier this year, announced its results for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026 after its board approved them on October 13, 2026. This article reports the figures as published in coverage of the results by Free Press Journal and Kotak Neo and explains the terms used. Where the two sources report slightly different premium measures, the difference is noted, and growth rates marked as calculated here are derived from reported numbers.

Profit

Profit after tax for the first half of fiscal year 2026-27 was ₹760 crore, up 26.5% from the same period a year earlier. The Free Press Journal's reading of the statutory filing gives the figure as ₹760.40 crore, up 26.4% from ₹601.35 crore. One crore is ten million rupees, so the half-year profit is about 7.6 billion rupees.

For the September quarter alone, profit was ₹374.22 crore against ₹299.26 crore a year earlier, an increase of 25%. It was 3.1% lower than the ₹386.18 crore reported in the June quarter. Profit before tax was ₹435.32 crore, up 25.4% from ₹347.01 crore. Basic earnings per share were ₹2.58 against ₹2.07.

Premiums

Net premium income for the quarter was ₹13,803.90 crore, up 16.6% from ₹11,843.10 crore, and for the half year it was ₹23,553.23 crore, up 15.8%, according to the Free Press Journal. Kotak Neo reports total premiums of ₹24,505 crore for the half year, up 15.3%. The two figures differ because one is net of reinsurance and the other is a broader total premium measure, and both show growth of around 15% to 16%.

Annualised premium equivalent, usually shortened to APE, is the standard way life insurers compare sales across product types. It counts regular premiums at their full yearly amount and single premiums at a fraction, often one-tenth, of the amount paid. APE for the half year was ₹4,935 crore, up 15.1%. For the September quarter it was ₹2,799 crore, up 15.6%.

Value of new business and margin

Value of new business, or VNB, is an actuarial estimate of the value that policies sold in a period are expected to create for shareholders after allowing for the cost of capital. VNB for the half year was ₹1,283 crore, up 22.3%. The VNB margin, which divides VNB by APE, was 26%, up from 24.7% a year earlier. A rising margin means each rupee of sales is creating more estimated value. The figure of ₹1,283 crore divided by ₹4,935 crore gives 26.0%, which matches the reported margin, calculated here.

VNB depends on assumptions about interest rates, lapses and costs, so a change in margin can reflect product mix, assumptions, or both. The coverage does not describe any change in assumptions.

The protection shift

The most notable item is the growth in protection. Protection APE for the half year was ₹1,155 crore, up 39.5%, and retail protection APE was ₹455 crore, up 47.2%. In the second quarter alone, protection APE rose 51.5% and retail protection APE rose 36.5%. Protection policies, such as term life cover, pay out only if an insured event occurs and typically earn higher margins than savings products. By comparison, linked savings APE rose 11.8% in the quarter, non-linked savings APE rose 6.7%, and annuity APE fell 0.6%.

Protection made up about 23% of half-year APE, calculated here by dividing ₹1,155 crore by ₹4,935 crore. New business retail sum assured, the total amount of cover sold to individuals, was ₹2.32 lakh crore, up 34.9%. The shift in mix is the likely explanation for the margin gain, although the coverage does not state this directly.

Balance sheet, claims and persistency

Assets under management were ₹3.29 lakh crore at September 30, 2026. The solvency ratio, which compares available capital with the amount the regulator requires, was 229.9%, up from 213.2% a year earlier. The regulatory minimum in India is 150%. The 13th-month persistency ratio, which measures the share of policies still in force a year after they were sold, was 84.5%. The company reported a claim settlement ratio of 99.3%, which it described as its best for a first half, and said eligible non-investigated individual claims were settled in an average of 1.1 days. It also reported no non-performing assets since inception.

Costs and investment swings

Not every line improved. Expenses of management, the costs of running the business including commissions, were ₹2,654.17 crore in the quarter, up 23.3%, which is faster than the 16.6% growth in net premium income. Faster cost growth than premium growth squeezes profit unless it is offset elsewhere. In addition, policyholders' net investment income was negative ₹2,123.29 crore, against a negative ₹226.67 crore a year earlier. That line likely reflects market movements on investments held for policyholders in unit-linked products, where the investment risk is borne by customers, so it does not translate directly into a loss for the company, but it does affect reported income and the premium totals investors see.

The Free Press Journal notes that the results were unaudited. Shares of the company closed at ₹447 on October 13, down 3.5% on the day, according to Kotak Neo.

How to read the results

Taken together, the figures describe a business that is growing sales at around 15%, growing the value of those sales faster than that, and building a stronger capital cushion. The main points to watch are whether protection can keep growing at current rates, whether costs continue to outpace premiums, and whether the margin of 26% can hold if the mix of products changes. Investors usually combine VNB, APE, solvency and persistency when judging a life insurer, because profit in any one quarter can be distorted by market movements and accounting rules.

Sources: Free Press Journal and Kotak Neo coverage of ICICI Life Insurance's September-quarter and half-year FY27 results, approved by the board on October 13, 2026. The results are unaudited. Growth rates labelled as calculated here are derived from the reported figures.
source_name: ICICI Life Insurance (September-quarter results approved October 13, 2026), as reported by Free Press Journal and Kotak Neo
image_alt: Insurance policy documents and a pen representing life insurance protection plans (illustrative)
key_points: First-half FY27 profit after tax was ₹760 crore, up 26.5%, and September-quarter profit was ₹374.22 crore, up 25% on the year but 3.1% lower than the June quarter.
Value of new business rose 22.3% to ₹1,283 crore and the VNB margin improved to 26% from 24.7%, while annualised premium equivalent grew 15.1% to ₹4,935 crore.
Protection annualised premium equivalent rose 39.5% to ₹1,155 crore for the half year, with retail protection up 47.2% to ₹455 crore, as annuity sales were flat.
The solvency ratio was 229.9%, up from 213.2% a year earlier, and the 13th-month persistency ratio was 84.5%, with a claim settlement ratio of 99.3%.
Policyholders' net investment income was negative ₹2,123 crore in the quarter, compared with a negative ₹227 crore a year earlier, and expenses of management rose 23.3%.
why_it_matters: ICICI Life is one of India's largest private life insurers, and its shift toward protection products, which carry higher margins than savings products, is a theme across the sector. The results show how a growing share of pure risk cover is lifting the value created per rupee of sales, even as expenses and market-linked investment swings weigh on the reported quarter.

title: eHealth Q3 Revenue Falls 60% as Medicare Season Looms
summary: eHealth reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $21.3 million, down 60%, and a net loss of $35.9 million as Medicare Advantage approved members fell 60%, while it reiterated full-year revenue guidance of $405 million to $445 million that depends on the annual enrollment period now under way.
description:
eHealth, Inc., a US online marketplace that sells Medicare Advantage, Medicare Supplement and other health plans on behalf of insurers, reported its third-quarter 2026 results on November 4, 2026. The company holds an earnings call on the day of release and trades on Nasdaq under the symbol EHTH. The headline numbers look weak, with revenue down by more than half, but the company's business is heavily seasonal and the release spends much of its space on what happens next. This article sets out the figures, explains the terms involved and shows what the full-year guidance implies, with calculations marked as made here.

The quarter

Total revenue for the third quarter was $21.3 million, compared with $53.9 million in the third quarter of 2025, a decrease of 60%. The GAAP net loss was $35.9 million against $31.7 million, and the net loss attributable to common stockholders, after items such as preferred dividends, was $50.4 million against $44.6 million. Adjusted EBITDA, a non-GAAP measure of operating earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, amortization and certain other items, was a loss of $39.9 million against a loss of $34.0 million.

Costs fell, but by less than revenue. Total operating costs and expenses were $67.6 million against $95.4 million, a drop of 29%. Total marketing and advertising expense was $10.9 million against $24.4 million, a drop of 55%. Operating cash flow was negative $11.2 million against negative $25.3 million, an improvement of $14.1 million. Net adjustment revenue, which captures changes in the company's estimates of commissions on policies written in earlier periods, was a positive $1.4 million, against a positive $12.2 million a year earlier.

Nine-month figures

For the first nine months of 2026, revenue was $142.9 million against $227.8 million, a decrease of 37%. The net loss was $64.2 million against $47.1 million, and adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $52.7 million against a loss of $35.6 million. Operating cash flow for the nine months was positive $19.6 million, against $10.6 million, an increase of 85%.

Members and unit economics

The main driver of revenue is the number of members whose policies are approved by insurers. Medicare Advantage approved members were 11,562 in the quarter against 28,645, a fall of 60%, and 91,764 for the nine months against 141,884, a fall of 35%. Total approved members across all products were 24,394 against 46,270, a fall of 47%. The company also estimates its total Medicare Advantage membership, the customers it has previously enrolled who generate recurring commissions, at 540,653 at September 30, down 7% from 579,914.

The release reports two lifetime value figures, which estimate the commission revenue the company expects to receive over the life of each policy after applying conservative constraints. Constrained lifetime value per Medicare Advantage approved member was $955 against $975, a fall of 2%. Per Medicare Supplement approved member it was $1,424 against $1,467, a fall of 3%. The constraint percentages were unchanged from a year earlier at 5.5% for Medicare Advantage, 4% for Medicare Supplement and 7% for Part D.

Acquisition cost moved the other way. Total acquisition cost per Medicare Advantage equivalent approved member was $2,156 against $1,489, an increase of 45%. That figure divides spending by the volume of approved members, so when volume falls faster than spending, the cost per member rises. Lifetime value of $955 against an acquisition cost of $2,156 is a gap that, on a one-quarter basis, looks unfavorable, but the third quarter comes before the enrollment season, so the comparison may look different once fourth-quarter results are reported.

Balance sheet

Cash, cash equivalents and short-term marketable securities were $88.1 million at September 30, 2026, made up of $57.3 million of cash and $30.8 million of securities. Commissions receivable, the commissions eHealth expects to collect from insurers in future periods and has already recorded as an asset, were $970.6 million, of which $208.8 million was current and $761.8 million non-current. The large receivable relative to cash is a feature of the model: revenue is recognized on an estimated lifetime basis when a policy is approved, while cash arrives over several years.

Guidance and what it implies

The company reiterated its full-year 2026 guidance. Revenue is expected to be between $405.0 million and $445.0 million, GAAP net income between $8.0 million and $25.0 million, adjusted EBITDA between $55.0 million and $75.0 million, and operating cash flow between negative $10.0 million and positive $12.0 million. Net adjustment revenue is expected to be between $17 million and $20 million.

Subtracting the nine-month totals from the full-year ranges gives the fourth quarter the company is implicitly forecasting. Revenue would need to be about $262 million to $302 million, adjusted EBITDA about $108 million to $128 million, and GAAP net income about $72 million to $89 million, all calculated here. In other words, a quarter that would be larger than the first three quarters combined on revenue. That outcome depends on the annual enrollment period, which for Medicare runs from October 15 to December 7.

Chief executive Derrick Duke said the company is seeing "strong consumer demand we are seeing at attractive lead costs," and that "The most important weeks of AEP are still ahead." The release says the company completed its preparations for the enrollment period successfully, and that it improved 90-day retention for the second-quarter 2026 Medicare Advantage cohort under its lifetime advisory model, while cross-selling of ancillary products nearly doubled in the third quarter compared with a year earlier.

Cost reductions

The company also repeated cost targets: more than $60.0 million in annual variable spending reductions and about $30.0 million in annual fixed cost savings. Together they would amount to more than $90 million a year, calculated here, if both are fully achieved.

How to read it

The third quarter of a Medicare broker is typically its smallest, and a year-over-year comparison is complicated by changes in the timing of marketing and enrollments. The more informative questions for readers are whether the fourth quarter delivers the volume implied by guidance, how the lifetime value per member develops, and whether the retention improvements the company reports hold for the cohort enrolled this autumn. Until the fourth-quarter results are published, the guidance is a statement of expectation rather than a result.

Sources: eHealth, Inc.'s third-quarter 2026 earnings release, filed as an exhibit to a current report with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on November 4, 2026. Figures labelled as calculated here are derived from the reported numbers and are not company statements.

title: EverQuote Q3 Revenue Rises 25% to Record $218 Million
summary: EverQuote reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $218.1 million, up 25.4%, with auto revenue up 20.8% and home and renters revenue up 70%, while adjusted EBITDA rose 41% to $35.5 million and net income was $18.2 million.
description:
EverQuote, Inc., which runs an online marketplace that connects people shopping for insurance with insurance carriers and agents, reported its third-quarter 2026 results on November 2, 2026. The company trades on Nasdaq under the symbol EVER and holds a conference call on the day of its release. Because carriers pay EverQuote when consumers request quotes or buy policies, the company's revenue is a useful indicator of how much insurers are spending on customer acquisition. This article reports the figures from the release, explains the terms used, and marks growth rates and ratios computed here.

Revenue by line

Total revenue for the third quarter was $218.1 million, compared with $173.9 million in the third quarter of 2025, an increase of 25.4%. Revenue from automotive insurance, the company's largest line, was $190.4 million against $157.6 million, an increase of 20.8%. Revenue from home and renters insurance was $27.7 million against $16.3 million, an increase of 70.0%. The company's remaining revenue category, labelled other, was negligible in both years.

Automotive made up about 87% of third-quarter revenue and home and renters about 13%, calculated here. Home and renters is a much smaller line but is growing more than three times as fast, which is shifting the mix.

For the first nine months, total revenue was $604.0 million against $497.2 million, up 21.5%. Automotive revenue was $534.8 million, up 18.9%, and home and renters revenue was $69.2 million, up 46.5%.

Profit and margin measures

Net income for the quarter was $18.2 million, or $0.49 per diluted share, against $18.9 million, or $0.50 per share, a decline of 3.8% in net income. The release attributes the lower figure to higher income taxes and a one-time item in the quarter. Adjusted EBITDA, a non-GAAP measure of earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, amortization and certain other items, was $35.5 million against $25.1 million, an increase of 41.4%. The company states that its third-quarter figure excludes a $4.0 million charge for the termination of a vendor contract.

Nine-month net income was $56.0 million against $41.6 million, up 34.8%, with diluted earnings per share of $1.53 against $1.10. Nine-month adjusted EBITDA was $94.9 million against $69.5 million, up 36.5%.

The company also reports variable marketing dollars, a measure of the revenue left after deducting the variable costs of acquiring traffic. It was $62.6 million in the quarter against $50.1 million, an increase of 24.9%, and $175.4 million for the nine months against $142.5 million, up 23.1%. Variable marketing dollars grew in line with revenue, which suggests the company did not have to give up margin to achieve the growth, although the release does not report a margin ratio.

Cash flow, balance sheet and buybacks

Operating cash flow for the quarter was $40.5 million, up from $19.8 million, and for the nine months it was $94.4 million against $68.4 million. Cash and cash equivalents were $229.1 million at September 30, 2026, up from $171.4 million at December 31, 2025, and the company had no outstanding debt.

The board approved a new share repurchase program of $50 million. The company did not repurchase any shares in the third quarter of 2026, compared with $21.0 million in the third quarter of 2025. For the nine months, repurchases totaled $29.0 million against $21.0 million a year earlier. The new authorization gives the company the option to buy back stock, but the release does not say when or whether it will do so.

Guidance

EverQuote gave guidance for the fourth quarter only and did not provide full-year guidance. It expects revenue of $213.0 million to $223.0 million, variable marketing dollars of $57.0 million to $60.0 million and adjusted EBITDA of $29.0 million to $32.0 million. The midpoint of the revenue range, $218.0 million, is almost the same as the third-quarter figure of $218.1 million, calculated here. That implies little sequential growth in the fourth quarter, though the release does not give the fourth-quarter result for 2025, so the year-over-year growth rate implied by guidance cannot be calculated from the document.

Management commentary

Chief executive Jayme Mendal said that "Carriers continue to maintain strong underwriting profitability and an appetite for growth." The company's chief financial officer, Joseph Sanborn, described the quarter as a record, with 25% revenue growth, and said the company is investing in artificial intelligence while generating strong cash flow. The release provides no industry data to support the comment on carriers' profitability, so it is best read as management's view rather than a measured fact.

What the results say about the insurance market

For readers outside the investment world, the results are interesting because of what they imply about auto and home insurers. Carriers spend heavily on marketing when they want more customers, and they spend less when claims costs squeeze underwriting results. After several years in which many auto insurers raised rates and restricted new business, a strong quarter for a marketplace that is paid by carriers suggests that many have returned to seeking growth. The 70% rise in home and renters revenue points in the same direction for property insurance.

There are limits to that inference. EverQuote's results also depend on its own share of carriers' budgets, the traffic it can buy at a reasonable cost, and competition from other comparison sites and from carriers' own advertising. The company's growth could therefore reflect gains in market share as well as an increase in carrier spending.

What to watch next

The next points to watch are whether fourth-quarter revenue lands within the guided range of $213 million to $223 million, whether the company uses its new repurchase authorization, and whether home and renters continues to grow faster than auto. Investors will also look at whether adjusted EBITDA stays in the guided range of $29 million to $32 million, which is below the $35.5 million of the third quarter.
